items.author: wdi-dave-roberts
items.body:
`ponytail-audit` and `ponytail-review` target *structural* slop: speculative abstraction, reinvented stdlib, dead flexibility, the kind you fix by deleting. But a very common shape of AI-generated slop has nothing structurally redundant to delete: over-defensive control flow (deeply nested condition ladders, redundant guards) and blanket `try/except` / `catch` wrappers that swallow uncertainty. The deletion-first ladder skips these because there's no unused abstraction to cut, yet a guard clause collapses the ladder and one boundary handler replaces the blanket catch.

The pass has to stay sur
items.title: ponytail-audit/review: no pass for over-defensive control flow or broad exception wrappers

The current Ponytail instructions strongly optimize for the shortest diff, fewest lines, and immediate deletion of abstractions. In a real configuration-loader task, that pressure produced more architectural complexity: policy leaked into callers, the public contract became indirect, and several small conveniences obscured the one interface the system needed.

## Summary

The Copilot hook configuration in `copilot-hooks.json` uses `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` in its `bash` commands:

```json
"bash": "node \"${PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/ponytail-activate.js\"",
```

```json
"bash": "node \"${PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/ponytail-mode-tracker.js\"",
```

When VS Code runs on Windows and connects to a Linux remote environment (WSL), the host expands `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` before invoking Bash. The resulting command can contain a Windows-style path, which is invalid in the remote Linux shell and causes Node.js to fail to locate the hook script.

Using `$PLUGIN_ROOT` in the Bash-specific c
items.title: Copilot Bash hooks resolve ${PLUGIN_ROOT} incorrectly in VS Code Remote

items.author: chindris-mihai-alexandru
items.body:
## Problem

`ponytail-review` relies entirely on LLM analysis to detect over-engineering in diffs. This is thorough but slow -- each review requires a full model inference pass. For large diffs or CI pipelines, this adds latency and cost.

## Proposed addition

A standalone `detectOverEngineering(text)` function that uses regex patterns to quickly flag known over-engineering signals **before** the LLM does deeper analysis. Returns `[{ pattern, alternative, snippet }]` -- actionable findings that map directly to ladder rungs 2-4.

### Patterns

| Regex | Ladder Rung | Native Alternative |
|----
items.title: feat: regex-based over-engineering pre-filter for ponytail-review

items.author: guyoron1
items.body:
**Bug**

`ponytail-mcp/index.js:12` passes `version: "0.1.0"` to the `McpServer` constructor:

```javascript
const server = new McpServer({ name: "ponytail", version: "0.1.0" });
```

However, `ponytail-mcp/package.json` declares `"version": "4.8.4"`. MCP clients that inspect the server version see a stale `0.1.0`, and this will need manual updating on every release — something easy to forget.

**Fix**

Read the version from `package.json` at startup:

```javascript
import { readFileSync } from 'fs';
const { version } = JSON.parse(readFileSync(new URL('./package.json', import.meta.url), 'utf8'
items.title: ponytail-mcp: McpServer version hardcoded to 0.1.0 instead of reading package.json
